title: chat-server: fit ChatMessagePush to a platform size limit
description: Oracle: jmap-chat-push-platform-guide.md L272-274: "Servers MUST NOT drop: `@type`, `accountId`, `state` (on the outer object), `messageId`, `chatId`, `chatKind`, `senderId`, `hasMention`, `mentionScopes`, `encrypted`." L283-285: "If a single minimal entry still exceeds the platform limit, servers MUST fall back to a plain `StateChange` for that subscription rather than sending an invalid or oversized payload." Droppable-field order (SHOULD) L252-262: bodySnippet, spaceId, sentAt, spaceName, chatName, senderDisplayName. Web Push limit oracle: jmap-push-platform-guide.md L498-499 "Servers MUST keep plaintext under **3993 bytes**". Current: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/push.rs builds the payload (build_chat_message_push) and truncates only bodySnippet to maxSnippetBytes; nothing fits the serialized payload to a byte limit or signals the StateChange fallback. Per JMAP-vjm0 payload construction stays in chat-server; the limit value is the caller's (delivery layer, JMAP-gxxm). Source: JMAP-x3lu audit.
acceptance_criteria: A pure helper takes a built ChatMessagePush and a max byte count, drops fields in the guide order, never drops the MUST-keep fields, and returns None when a minimal single entry still exceeds the limit (caller sends StateChange). Tests assert serialized length <= limit and the MUST-keep set against hand-written JSON.
notes: Spec 63e9d08 changed this area after implementation; follow-up in JMAP-0x0q.15 (check what batch 7 landed before re-doing).
close_reason: Committed and adversarially verified (batch 7); CI at 84a9b7bc
